# WaySlice

> Free, open-source, purely client-side analyzer for outdoor activity tracks (hiking, trail running, cycling). Supports GPX / FIT / TCX / KML / KMZ; all parsing and analysis run locally in the browser — no file ever leaves the device. No account, no ads, no tracking.

WaySlice (https://wayslice.com/) is built around the sector: the whole track tells you what happened, a sector tells you where it happened. Any part of a track can be sliced on the interactive map or the elevation profile and read like telemetry — speed, pace, grade, elevation gain and loss, 3D distance, heart rate, cadence, power and temperature — and every sector's data can be inspected or exported.

## Core facts

- Completely free and open source (MIT license); no ads, no accounts, no in-app purchases
- Purely client-side: parsing and analysis happen entirely in the browser; files are never uploaded — suitable for privacy-conscious outdoor athletes
- Supported formats: GPX, FIT (Garmin activities), TCX, KML, KMZ
- Core features: slicing any sector with telemetry-grade metrics, elevation profile with speed / pace / grade / heart-rate / cadence / power / temperature overlays, automatic sector split (by waypoints, distance or grade), dual-variable density analysis, heart-rate zones, metric and imperial units
- Exports a selected sector as GPX, csv, txt or md
- Interface languages: English, Deutsch, Español, Français, Italiano, 日本語, 한국어 — the UI follows the browser language by default and can be switched in the settings drawer
- Basemaps: OpenStreetMap, OpenTopoMap, CyclOSM, Esri World Imagery, Sentinel-2 cloudless and more, with street, outdoor, cycling, satellite and minimal dark variants
